content.text: The verifier's narrative confirms every substantive element of the finding — status, citation, absence of a redline, and the treatment of the failed checks as artifacts. The only outstanding signal is the `general-solicitation carve-out: failed` flag, which the same feedback expressly declares inapplicable. There is no defect left to repair, so the correct action is to re-affirm the finding rather than manufacture a change; inventing a non-solicit covenant to satisfy a carve-out probe, or redlining text that already benefits us, would both be wrong.

input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for every detection trigger ("shall not solicit", "solicit", "induce", "recruit", "employ", "hire") return no restrictive covenant, and I read the candidate locations in full to confirm - General (§ 30.1-30.8), Customer Responsibilities (§ 12) and Confidentiality (§ 16.1-16.5) contain no restraint on Customer's hiring. Section 12.3 runs affirmatively in our favour: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire any person responding to general recruitment and records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. That is the rule's preferred outcome (no non-solicit on Customer), so the fallback formulation (mutual, 12 months, personnel involved in the Services, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs) is unnecessary, and no redline is proposed for a provision that benefits our party. The deterministic checks for "duration =< 12 months" and "general-solicitation carve-out" report failed only because they probe for terms inside a covenant that does not exist; with nothing binding Customer there is no duration or carve-out to measure, so those results are artifacts rather than evidence of a deviation - and § 12.3's general-recruitment wording supplies the substance of a carve-out regardless. Noted but out of scope: § 12.4 restrains Vendor from marketing a service competing with Customer's analytics products, a restraint on the counterparty rather than on us, so it is not flagged here.
